transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because work has been... difficult lately. 

I manage health services, and... well, anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work—like the monthly reports, or trying to plan a multi-site event—I just sort of... hit a wall. I keep putting those things off. Even when I know they matter. So... yeah. That's mostly why I'm here.
Have you experienced this kind of trouble focusing and putting off tasks since you were a kid, or is this something that started more recently?

Um... no, it's not new. I guess it's... it's been going on since I was a kid. 

Even back in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but... that I was always daydreaming. I was always losing worksheets, too. I'd forget to turn in my homework unless my mom actually checked my backpack every night. So... yeah. It's not a recent thing.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... I'm just frustrated with the work stuff, I guess. But I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad.
Aside from the frustration with work tasks, do you often find yourself worrying excessively about various things in your daily life, even when there's no clear reason to?
No... not really. I mean, I worry about getting fired if I don't get my reports done, but... I don't just sit around worrying about random things for no reason.
